assessment_scope: All ten samples are objective_only. No audio listening, pronunciation judgment, MOS or native-speaker evaluation was performed.
scope_summary: Two independent models use approximately 5 h training and 1 h held-out validation each. Bounded training stopped at English step 8,842 and Telugu step 7,451. Final inference uses English 8842 with sentence context and ordinary energy conditioning (SIL zeroing OFF), and unchanged Telugu 2000. E1/E2a/E2b use contextual English input; E3/E4 use the trained-word fallback. All ten real WAVs and requested plots exist. This report is objective-only: no native listening, satisfactory pronunciation, naturalness or clean blind-test result is claimed.
cross_language_comparison: English WAVs average 5.211 s with 6.77% of pooled predicted duration assigned to SIL; Telugu averages 6.334 s with 25.00% SIL. Different text, voices and alignment prevent a controlled language-quality ranking. Final English assignment ASR WER/CER is 27.59%/11.38%, compared with 24.14%/8.98% for original step 7,000/word-level input; stronger fixed-validation performance did not imply uniformly better assignment recognition. Telugu remains 86.49%/24.89%, with substantial word-boundary and written/spoken-form effects. All current non-SIL phones have positive durations and written WAVs have zero PCM rail hits; these are integrity facts, not proof of good speech.
failure_cases: The original frozen checkpoint comparison remains inconclusive and the country-list duration gate remains failed. English step 8,842 ordinary-energy fixed-probe WER/CER is 15.38%/11.19%, better than step 7,000's 38.46%/30.60%. SIL zeroing improved those three probes further to 7.69%/2.99%, but worsened the five assignment prompts to 37.93%/14.97% versus 27.59%/11.38% with it OFF, so the override was rejected. A global duration multiplier was also rejected after both probe error rates worsened. Context corrects the input verb-vowel target, not encoded stress or all audible errors. Raw negative SIL-energy predictions persist in some samples. No threshold, raw prediction or checkpoint validation loss was rewritten to conceal these failures.
next_steps: Obtain native-listener assessment for every exact sentence, including rare words, noun/verb stress, dates and code-switching. Resolve English speaker identities and use a Telugu-trained aligner with checked boundaries. Separate voiced/non-SIL pitch evaluation from SIL/zero-duration conventions, and study unconstrained energy predictions without selecting per-sentence winners. Future generalization claims need new held-out material: these assignment and validation prompts have already informed post-hoc choices.

English.training_interpretation: Training total falls from 19.7317 to 1.5567; the last-100-step mean is 1.4998. Held-out total falls from 4.4130 to 3.6431, with minimum 3.3738 at step 1500. The bounded run ends at step 8,842; this is not a claim that the configured target or satisfactory speech quality was reached.
English.instability_or_overfitting: Training keeps improving after the validation minimum; final validation total is 0.2693 above that minimum. This plateau/gap is compatible with limited generalization or overfitting, not proof of a single cause. Training uses masked batch reduction while validation averages per utterance. Final validation pitch loss is 1.1972; the pitch criterion includes SIL and zero-duration positions, so it is not a voiced-speech F0 error score.
English.limitations: The 115 source demographic groups are not verified speakers; 114 occur in training and 106 in validation. The final 8,842/context/ordinary-energy recipe is selected for stronger fixed-validation recognition and the input-vowel correction, not for being the lowest assignment-ASR recipe or a quality-gate winner. SIL zeroing was rejected after the controlled assignment regression. Validation includes 8,051 SIL positions among 38,450 phones, including 3,319 zero-duration SIL targets; pitch-loss conventions remain a confound.

Telugu.training_interpretation: Training total falls from 21.9279 to 1.0588; the last-100-step mean is 0.9674. Held-out total falls from 3.8938 to 3.2523, with minimum 3.2036 at step 2000. The bounded run ends at step 7,451; this is not a claim that the configured target or satisfactory speech quality was reached.
Telugu.instability_or_overfitting: Training keeps improving after the validation minimum; final validation total is 0.0487 above that minimum. This plateau/gap is compatible with limited generalization or overfitting, not proof of a single cause. Training uses masked batch reduction while validation averages per utterance. Final validation pitch loss is 1.5208; the pitch criterion includes SIL and zero-duration positions, so it is not a voiced-speech F0 error score.
Telugu.limitations: The female single-voice subset avoids the English identity-proxy issue, but zero-shot Telugu alignment and collapsed acoustic classes remain. Step 2000 is retained after later WER worsens while CER improves. Validation has 4471 SIL positions among 36155 phones, including 1467 zero-duration SIL targets. High source-control WER and word-boundary effects limit ASR interpretation; no native listening was performed.
